utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Will you please call the case, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we have appearances, please, for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to the colleagues from the OTP, to everyone in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic, with legal assistants, Lana Deljkic and Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, sir. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just want to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Let us resume where we left off yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 776, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecutor showed you this document yesterday. This is a report from the security service of the 3rd Corps, dated the 3rd of July, 1995. You saw your initials there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document be scrolled down for the witness to look at that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed that you were, indeed, the author of the document. I want you to have a look at it to refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will remind you that the document describes a piece of intelligence, to the effect that the detachment members tried to solve the problem of their members who were captured. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document refers to -- to the various connections that the unit commander had via the Croatian police, the Croatian officer Zivko Totic, the civilian police in Travnik, all the way to the State Presidency. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I agree, and that's what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that nowhere in this text is the name of the commander of the staff of the Supreme Command mentioned as the possible connection of -- that the Mujahedin might have to solve their problems?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that's not what the document mentions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Having worked in the analysis department and dealing with pieces of information such as this one, you were able to see various documents referring to the Mujahedin and their connections. Have you ever seen a document where the Mujahedin were mentioning General Rasim Delic as a possible connection or as a contact that might help them solve a problem that they had?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never seen such a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this document away. Can the witness be shown document 777 -- or rather, Exhibit 777.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you this document yesterday. This document is from the security service department of the 3rd Corps, dated the 8th of July, 1995. You will recall that this speaks of the death of Kasim Celenka, who was a member of the detachment. Do you recall the document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the last paragraph of the document. You wrote the following: "We are going to request the security organ of the El Mujahedin Unit to submit a detailed report about the cause of the accident and the death of Kasim Celenka, and we are going to inform you of the information we learn in." Testifying about this document yesterday, you said that you made the document on the basis of a document you received from a subordinate unit. It is true, is it not, that this type of document, be it a document at your level, the 3rd Corps, or lower level units, contained a customary formulation when addressing subordinate units? The usual formulation was through the security organ of the unit, "Please report to us on this and that." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the El Mujahedin Detachment, this was a unit which, at different time periods, was establishment-wise a unit of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this: Did you ever receive from the security organ of the El Mujahedin Unit any report on any event?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the analysis department, we have -- we had never received a single document on security matters from the security organ of the El Mujahid Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you yourself have no knowledge about whether that unit had a security organ or not.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that unit had a security organ or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive information from the security organ of the El Mujahid Unit concerning this person by the name of Celenka?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever information I received, I passed it on; therefore, whatever I received from the security organ of a subordinate unit, I wrote about it and included it in the document I made.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The drift of my question is the following: Did you receive this detailed report about the causes of the accident and death of Celenka from the El Mujahedin Detachment after this particular document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The transcript seems to have stopped, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am struggling with mine. Mine has stopped, too. Are we the only two whose transcripts have stopped? Mine has stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, mine as well. Your Honour, I will repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It has stopped for some time. I have been trying to get it to start. I am advised that assistance has been called for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It looks like it may be some time before the transcription is corrected. Oh, there it goes. Okay. Now, Madam Vidovic, in fairness to you, there were quite a number of questions you asked after it stopped. I don't know whether you are able to go back to that point where it stopped and go over those questions again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at the point when the transcript stopped, you confirmed that you didn't know whether that unit had the security organ or not; and then I asked you the following question: As far as this report is concerned, this document that you have seen, I asked you whether you had ever received from the security organ of the El Mujahedin Unit any further information, a detailed report about the causes of death of Kasim Celenka. You answered my question, but please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't receive any detailed report or information from the security organ of the El Mujahedin Unit on this event.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can put this document away. Can the witness be shown another document, one more only. Your Honour, can the witness be shown Exhibit 770. Let us turn to page 14 of the statement in the English and page 17 of the Bosnian version; page 17 of the Bosnian and 14 of the English version. This is the Bosnian version. Can we have page 14 of the English version. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, here you see a photocopy of your military booklet. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It shows in which municipality you were listed on the military records. You have that on the right-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time -- or rather, in 1994 and 1995, the 3rd Corps entered its military conscripts into the military records of the relevant municipality. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In terms of regulations, a person was a military conscript only if it was entered into the military records of a given municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the second page of this -- or rather, the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the document shows up, I'll ask you this: The form in which we see now of that military booklet was in use and was in force until 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have the word "VES" on the left-hand side of this booklet. Can you explain for the Trial Chamber what that means.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "VES" means military -- military specialty unit of the records.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And we have a number next to that; right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Can the witness repeat his answer, please. The interpreters didn't catch his answer, and can the counsel and witness not overlap, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, the interpreters are complaining that you're overlapping. They didn't hear your answer, sir. Could you please repeat your answer. The question was: "And we have a number next to that; right?" That's when they lost you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, there is a number next to it, and it denotes a unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. I want the witness to look at the right-hand side of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that precisely in the way, in which we see this in your booklet, the participation of the conscript in various units was described in the booklet and certain time periods of that participation were certified in the booklet? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can exactly see here from what date up to -- up to which date you served in various units.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, this document that you have been showing, although attached to the witness's statement, it was not admitted yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like this to be admitted as a separate exhibit, the last document I showed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness's military identity document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 785.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. 785, okay. Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour, from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Spahic, thank you so much for coming to testify at the Tribunal. That brings us now to the conclusion of your testimony. You are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Fuad Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, we are advised the witness has not arrived yet. He will only arrive at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps if we could take a brief adjournment, I can see if I can make arrangements to get him here a little bit sooner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe before we do that, can we just do a small housekeeping? The Trial Chamber now renders its decision on the Prosecution's fourth motion for leave to amend its exhibit list filed on the 31st of October, 2007. In its motion, the Prosecution requests leave to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit list by adding a proposed exhibit attached to the motion as Annex A, which includes a list of cases from the archives of the Zenica Doboj cantonal prosecutor's office. The Prosecution submits that this list forms an integral part of the expected testimony of Witness Muris Hadziselimovic. The proposed exhibit was disclosed to the Defence on the 24th of December, 2007. On the 7th of November, 2007, the Defence orally responded to the motion by submitting that it did not oppose the motion. The Trial Chamber has considered the arguments advanced by the Prosecution in its motion. The Trial Chamber also noted that witness Muris Hadziselimovic is scheduled to testify on the 23rd of November, 2007. The Trial Chamber finds that it is in the interests of justice to allow the addition of the proposed exhibit to the Prosecution's exhibit list; and pursuant to Rule 54 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the motion is therefore granted. Shall we take a short break until we are advised. --- Break taken at 9.27 a.m. --- Upon resuming at 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In view of that little hitch, they suggested that maybe sit now until half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is a LiveNote problem again. Okay. We are advised that we can proceed, and the LiveNote will catch up with us. It is faster than us. I was going to suggest that, in order to cover the last time, we sit one and a half hours now, from now to half past 11.00; break until 12.00; and then sit with no more time off after that. Okay. Mr. Mundis, we will have the court usher escort the witness in first. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Good morning, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please stand up and make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be now be seated, Mr. Zilkic, and make yourself comfortable. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, sir, can you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: My name is Fuad Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zilkic, please, tell us your date of birth and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 10th of July 1963 in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, can you, please, briefly tell the Trial Chamber about your military career from the time that you first joined the military.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In 1983, I graduated from the military high school specialising in artillery in Zadar; after that, I worked in Benkovac as a non-commissioned officer. After that, in 1989, I enrolled into the military college in Zadar, which I graduated from in 1990, towards the end of 1990; and after that, as a second lieutenant, I worked in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For how long, sir, did you remain in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Until the 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After the 15th of April, 1992, Mr. Zilkic, what military force, if any, were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: After that, I left the JNA; and through Hungary and Croatia, I came back to Bosnia where, on the 18th of June, I reported to the Territorial Defence unit of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "the 18th of June," sir, what year are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zilkic, how long did you remain with the Territorial Defence unit?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Until the establishment of the 318th Mountain Brigade, where I became chief of artillery in that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall, sir, approximately, when the 318th Mountain Brigade was formed or established?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: 19th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long, Mr. Zilkic, did you remain as the chief of artillery in the 318th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Until the 8th of March, 1993, when I became the commander of the Municipal Staff of Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Zilkic, how long did you remain in the position of commander of the Municipal Staff of Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 320th Mountain Brigade was established towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, serve in the 320th Mountain Brigade, sir, once that unit was established at the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The municipal Territorial Defence Staff was transformed into the 320th Mountain Brigade, and I became the commander of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in the position of commander of the 320th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Until the end of 1994, when the two brigades - the 318th and 320th Brigades from Zavidovici - were merged into the 328th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what position, sir, did you hold in the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Commander also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long did you remain the commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, approximately -- the approximate date when the 328th Mountain Brigade was established?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I think in November of 1994; September or November 1994. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as the brigade commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade, Mr. Zilkic, to whom did you report?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: To the commander of the 35th Division, Colonel Fadil Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where was the headquarters of the 328th Mountain Brigade in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It was in the culture house in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the period 1995, how was the 328th Mountain Brigade structured in terms of subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It had five mountain battalions and other staff units, artillery, engineers, communications, logistics, anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, sir, in 1995 where the five mountain battalions of the 328th Mountain Brigade had their headquarters.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain Battalion was headquartered in the town of Zavidovici, its command was. It's forward command post was in Marici. It is a village close to their AOR. The 2nd Mountain Battalion was headquartered at Krcevine. It is a hamlet close to the village of Medevici, and it's very close to its AOR. The 3rd Battalion was in the village of Hajdarevici; the 4th in the village Livade. The 5th Battalion was headquartered in Boravnice, and its forward command post was in Curici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What combat operations, if any, did the 328th Mountain Brigade participate in during 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I would say that my brigade was a stationary brigade. And since all combat operations took part in its AOR, it partly took part in all combat activities, either through seconding part of its composition for attacks or a brigade which would take up the newly reached lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to clarify that answer, sir. When you say "seconding part of its composition for attacks," what are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about seconding a part of the manpower pursuant to orders of the 35 Division, which troops then took part in offensives, in offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To what unit or units did you second part of the manpower of the 328th Mountain Brigade to?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: To -- primarily to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you also said, just a few moments ago, that "the brigade would take up the newly reached lines," again, sir, what were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I think that all units which came to my AOR, to effect offensive activities, did so from the lines of defence of my brigade as the launch pad. And if they were successful in their assault, my unit had the duty to organise the newly reached lines in terms of organising the defence and manning those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Zilkic, when you say "I think that all units which came to my AOR," I would ask you: What units came to your AOR in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I can list you some. Some 30 units came from the composition of the Army of BiH: The 303rd, 314th, 330 Light, 375th, 7th Muslim, the Black Swans, and many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned a few moments ago the El Mujahedin Detachment, and I would like to ask you, if you can recall, when the first time you heard of that unit.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The first time I heard about them was when I was summoned by the division commander to his command post, where he introduced me to the commander of that unit. That was towards the end of 1995 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: At the beginning of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And who were you referring to when you said "the division commander"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fadil Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to which command post were you summoned?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I think that the command post was at the old municipality house at Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you said a few moments ago that the division commander introduced you to the commander of that unit, do you recall who that commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment was at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Abu Maali.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the names or identities of any other persons who attended this introductory meeting?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Abu Maali, Moatez, and the interpreter Aiman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was discussed at this meeting in the beginning of 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I did not speak to them. This was just an introduction. The commander had talked to them beforehand, then he invited me to be introduced. He did not issue me with a mission, but he told me that that unit was going to be in my area of responsibility for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which part of your AOR the El Mujahedin Detachment was going to be in?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, this was not discussed. This was just an introduction. After that, they contacted my units out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you elaborate upon how the El Mujahedin Detachment contacted your units out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: They were primarily entered into the range and elevation of Podsjelovo, the village of Livade, in that area where they were located, parts of that detachment were there. Contact was maintained through the 35th Division. Their requests were handled through the 35th Division. The commander issued me with orders, and I complied with those orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You mentioned the elevation of Podsjelovo. Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether any efforts were made in 1994 with respect to Podsjelovo.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In June, towards the end of June and the beginning of July 1994, there was a major combat to capture elevation 715 at Podsjelovo. The fortune changed hands. We were successful for a time; the enemy for another. The combat lasted for 20 days with substantial losses on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was the result of these operations in June and July 1994 with respect to Podsjelovo?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: We lost some territory there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1994, which armed force controlled the elevation points on Podsjelovo?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1994, I recaptured that lost territory with my units. So we held the elevation 715, the elevation 726; and the others to the left [as interpreted] of it, they were held by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And which elevations -- when you say "the others to the left were held by the enemy," which elevation points are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: To the right of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry. Which elevation points to the right were held by the enemy?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Starting with the Humka elevation 726, 2702, 2706 [as interpreted]. This is a natural range. It's a dominant position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. I think there's an error in the transcript, sir. Can you repeat the three elevation points that were held by the enemy at the beginning of 1995.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Elevation 726 named Humka, then 702 and 706.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: These three elevation points, 726, 702, and 706, how long were they held by the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Until the 25th May 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what happened on that day, sir, 25th May 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: On that day, the El Mujahid with parts of our units captured those elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, "parts of our units," can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: El Mujahid -- El Mujahid sought parts of our units to reinforce their ranks, to effect offensive operations on the basis of their requests. The vision commander determined which units will second how many men for those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You mentioned a few moments ago or we discussed this introductory meeting at the beginning of 1995. Other than that meeting, sir, did you ever have any subsequent meetings with the leaders of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I had some three or four meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall, with specifics, any of these subsequent three or four meetings?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: These were meetings at the division commands which were attended by all unit commanders; among others, commanders of the El Mujahid. We had short briefings. If the topic to be discussed was the preparation of combat activities, we would brief the commander on whether we were ready, whether we had made the preparations as ordered, in terms of manpower, troops. They were there. The command of the El Mujahid were there, but they did not brief the commander, and they would stay behind, most probably, to sort out the details with the commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you refer to the "commanders of the El Mujahid," who are you talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You said a few moments ago, at these meetings at the division command, all unit commanders attended; and then you went on and said "among others, commanders of the El Mujahid." I'm asking you who those El Mujahid commanders that you referred to were.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The commander, Abu Maali; Moatez; the interpreter, Aiman; and the other commanders were the commanders of the 327th, 328th, 329th Brigades, and other units that were to be part of an -- an attack or a combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the specific dates or general time periods in which these three or four subsequent meetings took place?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I remember the meeting of the 10th of September at Panorama, and I remember another meeting at Elektron, which is a factory close to Maglaj. There may have been more, but I presently cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the approximate date of the meeting at Elektron near Maglaj?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. This was after the 15th of September, when we started operations deep into the Ozren area. It was a briefing attended by the commander of the 3rd Corps, where missions were handed down for subsequent operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: These two meetings that you've told us about in September, what year were those, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to focus your attention, Mr. Zilkic, on the meeting at -- on 10 September 1995 at Panorama. Do you recall, approximately, what time that meeting took place on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I remember that it took place in the evening hours; maybe 2000 hours, around that time. I cannot be specific, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was Panorama?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It was a restaurant close to Zavidovici, which the division sometimes used as their forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this meeting on 10 September 1995 at approximately 2000 hours in Panorama, do you recall who attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The corps commander was there with a part of his staff, the division commander with part of his staff, and commanders of the units that were effecting activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at that time, sir, who was the corps commander that you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, which commander or commanders of the El Mujahedin Detachment were present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: All meetings which I attended, El Mujahedin was represented by Abu Maali; Moatez; and the interpreter, Aiman, except for one case where another interpreter was there, Abu Hamza.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the meeting that Abu Hamza attended?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I can't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this meeting on 10 September 1995 at Panorama in the evening, what was the topic of discussion?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Primarily on the subsequent tasks, tomorrow's tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What were the tasks that were discussed concerning 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Continuation of offensive activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say "continuation," Mr. Zilkic, when did these offensive activities commence?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Well, they started in the early morning of the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what happened on the 10th of September, 1995 in terms of these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I know that immediately after the commencement of the attack, El Mujahid captured the elevation of Paljenik within seven minutes. This is what I knew. I did not know at that time which positions our other units reached. Only later in the afternoon, I could see from my observation post the linking-up of the 2nd and 3rd Corps units in the area of Prokop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where was your observation post on that day?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: At elevation point 551.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt? Is there a problem? THE GUARD: She doesn't feel well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, are you going to deal with this witness, or is it she who's dealing with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness is being dealt with by Madam Vidovic. I'm not sure why she left. I was just heard from the security guard there that apparently she doesn't feel very well. I wasn't aware of the problem. I'm afraid I can't assist the Court really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. What do you want to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Madam Vidovic is going to return very soon, I'd be happy for the witness to proceed, but without -- I'm completely in the dark as to whether it's a serious problem or just something that can be dealt with momentarily. I'm in the hands of the Court. Either I can go and try and find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could, please, or if your assistant can help. Do you think you can help? Thank you very much. Just find out how long she will be and come and tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think under the circumstances that's the most prudent course of action, Your Honour. Thank you. Perhaps, I could just take this brief moment to inform the Trial Chamber I've discussed with the Defence some issues concerning scheduling, and a new schedule was circulated at the end of the last break with respect to next week's witnesses. The Trial Chamber's legal officer has been provided with a copy of that schedule. We're trying to make up a little bit of lost time, also with an eye towards the videolink that's scheduled on the 20th, which is, of course, not something that's movable. So, I'll just alert everyone to that fact, but the schedule has been circulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic, are you okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't look it, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the flu, and I'm running a high temperature, but I think I can bear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do tell us when you are not able to bear it. Okay? Okay. Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, I'd like to return to what we were talking about just a few moments ago. You told us, as reflected on page 18, lines 8 through 10, that immediately after the commencement of the attack, El Mujahid captured the elevation of Paljenik within seven minutes. And my question to you, sir, is: Were any units of the 328th Mountain Brigade involved in the capture of Paljenik?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: None of them were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's return then, sir, to the meeting on that evening. What do you recall, if anything, was discussed about the continuation of the operations that had commenced on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I can only say that this was a more relaxed atmosphere thanks to the successes achieved at the front line. It mostly had to do with further advancement toward the Kvrge feature, where we had the task of linking up with the units of the 2nd Corps on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, whether any taskings were given to the El Mujahedin Detachment at this meeting on the 10th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I was never present when they were being -- were being issued tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn, then, sir, to the operations on 11 September 1995. Where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Initially, I was also at the observation post 551, from where I was following the fighting around the Djurici elevation, Djurici Vis. After that, I went to the Gaj feature, from where I also followed the advancement of our units. When I saw that they were approaching the Kvrge feature, I set off toward 685 feature in order to reach the line I was supposed to reach on that day pursuant to the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which battalions of the 328th Mountain Brigade, if any, were involved in operations on 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: None of my battalions took part in these attacks. My entire unit was tasked with taking up the newly reached positions and with carrying out engineering work on these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What units of the 3rd Corps were involved in those attacks on 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: All the manoeuvre battalions were involved in them, that is to say, five manoeuvre battalions; elements of the 329th also took part; also of the 327th, I believe; the 7th Muslim; the, as we called them, Rekic's Specialists also took part in that; the sabotage battalion; and there were probably some other units. I can't recall at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, receiving any reports from your battalion commanders, oral reports from your battalion commanders, on 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I received the report from the commander of the 5th Battalion, Mr. Ahmet Sehic, to the fact that there were prisoners, that his unit had captured some men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, sir, for the benefit of the transcript, can you repeat the name of the commander of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmet Sehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time you received this report from Mr. Sehic on 11 September 1995, that his battalion had captured some men?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't recall at what time the first call took place. It was followed by a second call at around 1400 hours, when he reported to me that members of the El Mujahid Detachment had taken the prisoners away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's focus, sir, on the first call. Do you remember what you told Mr. Sehic with respect to these prisoners when he informed you about them?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: He told me that there were 40 to 50 prisoners, and I think he requested for a vehicle. I asked him which of his commanding officers were there, and he said that his deputy were there, as was the company commander. I told him to go there personally and to carry out the task, as per the order; meaning that he should comply with the order instructing everyone how to treat prisoners, and that he should be there to give a helping hand to the deputy and the company commander, who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, where these prisoners were on 11 September 1995 when you received this first call from Mr. Sehic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In the area of the village of Kesten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After this first call, you told us you received a second call.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that was around 1400 hours. What exactly did Mr. Sehic tell you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't recall his exact words, but he reported to me. He said the commander of the El Mujahid had taken away the prisoners --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: He said, "Commander, the El Mujahid had taken away the prisoners."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He told me that there were incidents, that my men drew weapons at them but that they were unable to do anything, and that the El Mujahid took the prisoners away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to correct the transcript. Page 26, lines 9 and 10, perhaps the Prosecutor can clarify this with the witness. It is entered in the transcript he said, "Commander, the El Mujahid..." It seems that's at least how it transpires on the transcript, that the commander of the El Mujahid had taken away the prisoner, but he said something else that. The El Mujahid had taken away the prisoners, or perhaps I misunderstand what is written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. If you will look at -- let's stop this thing so you can see it. If you look at line 10-- let me look at this one. If you look at 7, line 7, page 26: "I don't recall his exact words, but he reported to me. He said the commander of the El Mujahid had taken away the prisoners --" The interpreter then says: "Interpreter's correction: He said, 'Commander, the El Mujahid had taken away the prisoners.'" So there is a correction there. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all right. Thank you, Your Honour. I couldn't see this on my screen. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, when the 5th Battalion commander, Ahmet Sehic, reported to you that the Mujahedin had taken the prisoners away, were you concerned about that situation?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Of course, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Well, up to that point, it had never happened that somebody would kidnap prisoners from someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did you do with the information you received from Mr. Sehic concerning these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: After I received the first word from the battalion commander that the prisoners had been taken away, I informed my superior over the radio set that I had with me; and then he told me, "Very well. Let's proceed according to plan."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, whether these -- these prisoners were the subject of any subsequent discussions between you and Mr. Sehic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the evening hours at the forward command post of the 1st Battalion, which was at Sjenokos, after I came down from the lines at the Kvrge feature, I called him to recount everything to me in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us just a moment ago that after you received the word from Mr. Sehic, you informed your superior. Who were you referring to, sir, as your superior?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The division commander, Mr. Fadil Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, whether there were any subsequent discussions or briefings with Mr. Hasanagic, where the topic of these prisoners was discussed?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that. But I have to say that those were the days of intense combat activities, and I reported to the superior command on everything that had happened at the time in detail because I felt that I personally could do nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown Exhibit 480.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could go to the fourth page of the document in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Whose signature is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could please go to the bottom of page 2 in the Bosnian and the middle of page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I draw your attention, sir, to the final bullet point, the second bullet point under paragraph number 4. What is the information in that section of the document based upon?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Out of the command-and-control system, where combat reports were written every day and sent to the superior command, they were written on the basis of the reports received from the battalion commanders out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And my specific question, sir, is: This second bullet point under paragraph number 4, what was the source of the information contained therein?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: A report from the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we no go to the top of page 2 in the Bosnian and to the middle of page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see that part of the document, sir, the second paragraph with the star that says "Activities of the Command"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this is in the middle of the English page or toward -- a little bit below the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you take a look at that paragraph, sir: "Last night and this morning a meeting was held at the operations centre of the 328th Mountain Brigade."

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see reference to officers of the El Mujahid Detachment attending this meeting or meetings?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you present at that meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I can't say that I was not, but I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page of the document in both English and B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This document is dated 13 September 1995. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, you don't remember the meeting or meetings referred to in the paragraph we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zilkic, do you know where the El Mujahedin Detachment had its headquarters or any of its command posts during 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't. I know some of the locations where they were headquartered -- where they before billeted, but I never knew where their command post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where were the locations where they were billeted that you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In my area of responsibility, there was always a part of the units in the village of Livade, and I am primarily referring to the men who conducted reconnaissance along the lines of defence. I know that they had their own camp at the 13th Kilometre

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How did you know they had a camp at the 13th Kilometre?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew that from various documents, and I was there. I was living there, I know the place, and I could see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked as PT2038, PT2038.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the document on the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is, please.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a regular daily combat report which my unit sent to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 3 of the document in Bosnian, and we can stay on the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Whose signature is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now if we could go back to the first page in the Bosnian, and now please go to page 3 in the English. If we could scroll down on the Bosnian, and we actually need -- we need the top part, actually, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- above paragraph 3, there are a number of bullet points. Do you see the one that makes reference to "Engineering"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you see the reference there, sir, to "Engineering consolidation of the defence line of the 2nd Mountain Battalion"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, sir, on the reference to "13th kilometre" that's reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I said that elements of the units of El Mujahid had a camp at the 13th Kilometre. Some of my engineering units did some works with construction machinery because it mentions road maintenance here, and they had some machinery that they used for the purposes of the El Mujahid Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be tendered into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 786.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT2094, PT2094.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that document is coming up, Mr. Zilkic, during 1995, where did the 328th Mountain Brigade have communication centres?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The main communications centre was at the command post of the brigade at Zavidovici, and the other operations centres were located as appropriate for the combat activities. They were normally at forward command posts. According to this document, there is an operations centre at the village of Imamovici...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: A communications centre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]... where you can see that it started working.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where do you see that on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In item 1.3, it says: "The communications centre of 328 Mountain Brigade at Zavidovici at the culture hall." Then: "The communications centre of the 328th Mountain Brigade at Zavidovici [as interpreted], culture hall, as of the 23rd of May, 1995, 1200 hours".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Does that say "Zavidovici," or does it say "Imamovici"? The line that refers to the 23rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you -- can you comment upon the question of the Judge, Mr. Zilkic? Where was the -- where was the communications centre established as of 23 May 1995 at 1200 hours?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: At the village of Imamovici, which was to the left from the elevation 715, in people's houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 787.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, do you or did you in 1995 have any direct contact between yourself and the commander or commanders of the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Apart from the meetings at the 35th Division, I had no meetings with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've told us, sir, about receiving orders to second personnel from your brigade and its battalions to the El Mujahid Detachment. Did you or your brigade provide any other form of logistical support to that unit in 1995, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We offered them logistics support whenever ordered to do so by the division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What kind of logistics support, Mr. Zilkic, did your brigade or its battalions provide to the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Well, we saw an example where we fortified some positions. There were examples where we were supposed to establish communication or a communication system; then there were examples where we would dislocate heavy weapons pursuant to their requests; and then there were requests to repair motor vehicles. There were requests to supply them with food, and many other things that they requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, so that we're clear, how did -- how did these requests come to your attention?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Through the 35th Division in the form of an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we now take a look at PT2232, PT2232.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Zilkic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a regular daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Of what unit?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Of the 328th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please focus on the bottom half of the Bosnian, and go to page 3 in the middle in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, approximately, just below the middle of the page in Bosnian, do you see the bullet point that begins "El Mujahid Detachment"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you take a look at that bullet point to familiarise yourself with what's in this report, and can you then comment upon what you've put in this report, please.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In this report, it can be seen that there was a request of the El Mujahedin from the 35th Division, to the effect that a B-1 gun to be removed from Mramorje, from the position of the 2nd Mountain Battalion to another location, in keeping with their plans for further combat operations; and, whereby, I report that by relocating that gun, that would weaken the position of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, what a B-1 gun is.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It is a 76-millimetre artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 2 in the Bosnian and page 6 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I draw your attention, sir, to paragraph 5, that talks about logistics, subparagraph 2. Do you see the reference there, sir, to an FAP truck?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is being reported in this part of your daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Nothing, except what is written here, that they repaired their vehicle, which was in the composition of the El Mujahid Detachment, which was broken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 788.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can we now take a look at PT2359.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a regular monthly combat report that we submitted at the end of the month to our superior command, including all the specified elements of such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to the last page of this document in -- in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who signed this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I did. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 3 in the English and page 2 in the original, and go to the top in the Bosnian. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, can you please read the first paragraph of -- under heading number 2, "Brigade forces."

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: "During this reporting period, the main body of our forces carried out decisive defence on the line of defence; and with joint forces of the 35th Division of land army, according to a plan of the El Mujahedin Detachment, between the 21st and 27th July of 1995, we conducted offensive operations. Offensive combat operations were carried out on the main axis, Sjenokos-Vis, and on to the secondary axis, Podsjelovo-Kvrge."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you recall, sir, what the objective was of the 328th Mountain Brigade with respect to this time period, 21 to 27 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The goal of the -- the goal of the 328th Mountain Brigade could only have been to maintain the lines and fortifying of the lines during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we now go to page 3 in Bosnian and page 6 in English. I want the top parts of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, do you see, sir, the heading "Focus of engagement of brigade forces"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the first -- the first sentence under that heading, can you comment upon what you wrote there in this report?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: "As in all situations, the focus of members our forces was focused on decisive defence and to set aside forces for combat operations according to the El Mujahid plan." I said that whenever El Mujahid were to launch offensive operations, they would seek parts of our units that would be seconded and re-subordinated to them; and they were trained by them, after which they would carry out combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now if we could go to the bottom of the document in -- in English, but it's fine in -- in the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, the second big paragraph under this heading which refers to the period between 21 and 24 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Can you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the second large paragraph under the heading "Focus of engagement" that discusses action between 21 and 24 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: You mean unit activities or the focus of engagement? Could you please clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: "Focus of engagement." Do you see the little -- the little dot where there would be -- where there's two holes in the document? Do you see those little circles on the left-hand side? Yes, right there. Right where that's been highlighted, that -- that part of the document, sir. Can you take a quick read through that paragraph. You don't need to read it out loud, just to yourself.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment upon that part of your document which says "led by the El Mujahid."

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This concerns a continuation of the Proljece operation, where the goal was to capture elevations Gaj, Jezero, Jasicka Kosa, Rudenjak, Markovica Vis, all the others cited here, where our units - and, by this, I mean parts of the units that were by the order of the 35th Division seconded and re-subordinated to the El Mujahedin Detachment - they took part in this area in combat operations, because this is a monthly report outlining all the activities carried out by my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What does it mean when you wrote "led by the El Mujahid"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: After Proljece in 1995, which means after 25th of May, where they had achieved a major success by capturing the elevation of Podsjelovo, I don't know what their tasks were, but what I did know is that they were preparing for further actions. And in all subsequent combat operations engaged our units, parts of our units that the El Mujahid trained, but there were the driver of the -- such combat operations. They were conducted under their plans, and they were the first to engage in combat. So they were the ones to break through the enemy lines, to make this matter clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the bottom part of this document and the bottom of page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see where it says "Activities of units"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There's reference there to "soldiers conducted training at the 9th km, according to the El Mujahid Detachment's plan." I'd like to ask you, sir, if you can comment upon what you wrote here in this document.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is that all about, this training at the 9th Kilometre according to the El Mujahid Detachment's plan?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: For the planning of subsequent combat operations, the El Mujahid Detachment made an assessment of how many of our troops they needed for such combat operations. And as per the division commander's schedule and order, all units had to second some troops to be re-subordinated to the El Mujahid Detachment, where they were trained - I never attended that training personally - which would last between five to seven or ten days. And, primarily, that training consisted of religious training and the bonding of our troops with the people from -- of Arabic origin, so that they be as compact a unit as possible during offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What do you mean "so that they would be as compact a unit as possible"? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: By this, I primarily mean that they were psychologically primed, telling them that the enemy was nothing special, that all combat actions are possible to carry out. Of course, they cited themselves as examples. They worked on the morale of our units mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This reference to training at the 9th Kilometre, do you know where that training took place, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It was the area of the school in the area of the 9th Kilometre, where before the war there was a school building, school yard, and a gym, and there was some flat ground, empty ground around it. When -- while manoeuvre battalions were established, our 4th Manoeuvre Battalion conducted their training there. This location was away from the lines of defence, so that training could proceed without hindrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, the name of the village or hamlet that's at the 9th Kilometre?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Cardak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 789.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is -- is Cardak, sir, also known as Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Well, Gostovici encompasses -- Gostovici itself is a river 18 kilometres long. But when we referred to Gostovici, we divided that into Gornji Gostovic and Donji Gostovic, and the local communities numbered 50; meaning 50 villages, hamlets. Ten of them were larger villages, and the rest were hamlets with five, ten houses each.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we now take a look at PT2374, PT2374.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see this document on the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could scroll down in the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who signed this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a report to my superior command, to the effect that the enemy is conducting an artillery and infantry attack in the area of my 4th Battalion in the area of elevation 406 [as interpreted]. So this was what happened that day. We spent a large amount of ammunition, and we report to the superior command that we rejected that attack and that we need and requisition replenishment of materiel and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, the transcript reflected that this concerned the area of your 4th Battalion in the area of elevation 406. Can you point us to that part of the document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Elevation 706, in the area of elevation 706.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it said so in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 2 in the English, but stay on this page in the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, in the middle, approximately the middle of the page, there's a reference to "El Mujahid/MB-120." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell -- can you tell the Trial Chamber what you were reporting in this part of your document.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: During the enemy's attack, since this was a sizable attack, parts of the El Mujahedin Detachment, primarily mortars 120 millimetres that were located at Livade, provided support to my troops. This most probably was at the request of the scouts or parts of the El Mujahedin people from the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion, because I could not order those mortars from the El Mujahedin to be used, but I do report to my superior command that this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And so I take it, sir, from that answer, that "MB-120," is that 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 790.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think we have time for one more document before the break. If the witness could please be shown PT2380.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Zilkic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please quickly go to page 4 in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask you if you recognise the signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is this document, Mr. Zilkic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: As all the others, this was a regular daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please look --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And we could go back to page 1 in the English, to the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see under paragraph number 2, sir, again, there's reference to "El Mujahid Unit" in that paragraph? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you tell us what you're reporting in this paragraph with respect to the El Mujahid Unit.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: As part of my tasks of my units which effected decisive defence, it follows - and this is what I report on - how many members of my units would man the lines of defence; what was the -- our strength and status of our troops; how many people we had from other units and how many of them were ready for manning the lines of defence, because my unit was a large one. These units referred to are those that should intervene in the case of an enemy's attack. They were in the -- in the reserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 2 in both versions of the document. We'll need the middle in Bosnian and the very bottom in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, where it says "Additional information" and then "Stand-by schedule"? Do you see that, Mr. Zilkic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, there's a subheading with a star by it that says "Additional information," and under that, "Stand-by schedule." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you tell us what you're reporting in this part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It does carry over onto page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After we'd lost some territory, particularly the feature 685, and given that my unit could not have reserve troops primarily in terms of weapons but also in manpower, my troops were exhausted after manning the lines of defence for months on end. At my requests, I demanded that, in certain features and places, that we have stand-by units. Taught from the experience of the activities around the 685, I report to the commander how many units are where, being in stand-by mode.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. Before it is removed, can we turn to page 3 in the English, please, because we haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 791.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. The document may move.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This would be an appropriate time for the recess, Your Honours, for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask that the witness now be shown PT2434, PT2434.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
