utterances.text: Who signed this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It's an interim combat report sent to the superior command, wherein I report to them about the fact that the El Mujahedin sabotage unit carried out a successful sabotage action in the area of the feature 673.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is this -- if you know, sir, what is this sabotage unit of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It is mentioned here, a sabotage group, but it could be any one of the members of the detachment which, starting from my defence lines, go into the depth of the territory and carry out a sabotage action. This was probably written on the basis of the reports from the field; that's the say, the 4th Mountain Battalion. It is on the basis of their report that I pass this information on to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 791.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I apologise, 792.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown PT2450, PT2450.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to take a look at this document, and can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This document, just as any other document coming from the superior command down to me, is an order ordering for me to give an assignment to 200 men out of my unit to carry out the evacuation of the wounded. It says here that this is to be done for the purposes of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, receive this order of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What steps, if any, sir, did you take to carry out this order?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I assessed the units and decided how many men could be taken out of each of them, and I told the commanders that the men I selected should be at a previously designated place at a time previously set.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say you told the commanders that the men you selected should be at a designated place at a certain time, which commanders are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to my battalion commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And earlier, sir, you testified about seconding personnel to the El Mujahedin Detachment. Is this the type of order under which you would make those secondments?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This, too, was one of such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt. These casualties that are being collected and evacuated, are they from your army or from the enemy army or from both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this primarily refers to our casualties, because every offensive action normally implies that as a result of that there would be killed and wounded. They relied on their commanders in this case to bring in the men necessary to evacuate the wounded, to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We would tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 793.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown PT2507, PT2507.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This document of the 35th Division issues an order to me for the purposes of the El Mujahid Detachment, which had some of its units in my line of defence, that elements of the El Mujahid Units should be pulled out of the area of combat activities because of upcoming combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if I understood you, sir, you said that elements of the El Mujahid Unit should be pulled out of the area of combat activities because of upcoming combat activities. Is that what you said, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I said that they have to be pulled out of the stand-by mode, so to speak, the area for stand-by, because you'll remember that we looked at earlier documents referring to "stand-by forces." Forces that are to be on the -- on stand-by are normally pulled out of the zone of active combat into the stand-by area, which is the 9th Kilometre. This was where they normally went to rest and awaiting for orders to engage in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, there's reference in paragraph -- in the introductory paragraph and in the first paragraph to "Asim Camdzic Company." Can you tell the Trial Chamber what the Asim Camdzic Company is or was.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This unit varied in size, between 50 and 80 men, who were part of my composition, and I used them for interventions along the lines of defence. However, the unit was primarily composed of soldiers who were, let's say, practicing believers, more devout believers, and so they were in that way similar to the soldiers from the El Mujahedin Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 794.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown PT2511, PT2511.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: My Chief of Staff, Hidajet Vrabac [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document relates to.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This document is a follow-up on the previous order to pull out the Asim Camdzic unit deep behind the lines for rest and to put the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion in its stead, to be on stand-by and reserve for these units. Therefore, the superior command is being informed about the fact that the previous order was complied with and the way in which it was complied with is described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 795.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We ask that the witness now be shown the document 481, marked for identification. Perhaps if we could scroll down or see the full part of the first page in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you tell us, please, what this document is, sir.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that before I see its contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this before we go to the next page: Who signed this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we now go to the next page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The title itself says that it's an analysis of preparation and execution of combat activities during Operation F-95, and this is the operation that commenced on the 10th of September. That's what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of this document?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This document was made on the 16th of October; therefore, after the end of combat activities. Probably the division command ordered that an analysis of all combat activities be made. We complied with that and submitted an analysis. What was meant by that was that one ought to present the good sides and the bad sides of these activities, strengths and weaknesses of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is now admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. I guess it will be Exhibit number 481.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, Exhibit number 481.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zilkic, in response to my last question, you mentioned the end of combat activities, and I'd like to ask you, sir: Do you recall approximately when the combat activities ended in the Vozuca area?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I know that, in the Vozuca area, the combat activities ended on the 15th of September; however, in deep in the Ozren area, the activities ended on the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown PT2714.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I do; although, it's quite unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is, sir.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is an order of the General Staff addressed to the brigades and division commands on the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which -- which cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It speaks of the cessation of all combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 796.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I haven't had time to raise my objection before the admission of the document. First of all, we didn't have the opportunity to look at page 2. Secondly, I don't believe that the foundation was laid for the admission of this document through this witness. Could we please have the document back on our screens again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness did mention that the activities in the, as he put it - this is on line 19 of page 49 - "in deep in the Ozren area, the activities ended on the 10th of October." That's what this document relates to, at least in part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Vidovic is also raising the point of seeing page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yeah. We can certainly see page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to see page 3 as well in the English. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only see a general order to the corps and some divisions, which definitely do not include the 35th Division. Besides, I don't see the mention of either Ozren or Vozuca anywhere in this document, or are we perhaps speaking of a different document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, that's what I just indicated, that -- that the document relates to, at least in part, cessation of hostilities, a cease-fire on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands. If the -- if the document is not to be admitted, we'll just move on. I can't take it any farther with this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I could hear, the witness said that on the 10th of October, the combat activities ended in Ozren. It is quite evident that the order is dated the 11th of October. That's the reason why I intervened. I don't see that the witness has any connection with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the first page of this document, please. Sir, what made you stop hostilities on the 10th of -- the 10th of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order of the commander of the 35th Division, based on the order of the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you receive the order of the -- of the commander of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly, but I believe I did. Cessation of hostilities was ordered. Whether it was ordered in writing or orally, it was ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you ever receive this document that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Mundis, we can't admit the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine. We'll move on. Thank you. Can the witness now be shown Exhibit PT2935. Perhaps we should have this document marked for identification, since it was discussed at least tangentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then it will remain marked for identification as Exhibit 796.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This -- I should also indicate for the record that PT2935 consists of a number of different maps. I'm not sure if it would be best to -- well, we'll take it one step at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, do you recognise the map on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this map is, sir.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a map of the decision of the commander of the 328th Brigade for defence, which is probably accompanied by a written order to defend the lines. Here, one can see all the elements of the combat disposition of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is the -- what is the date of this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The 1st of March of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, sir, is this map accurate as of that date?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: As soon as I signed it, it ought to be correct and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, sign it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can make out the signature, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next map in this PT.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this map on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this map is.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a map accompanying the order of the commander of the 35th Division to launch offensive activities.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Can the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This relates to Operation Farz 95.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell -- can you tell us what this map is.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: One in a series of maps on the basis of the decision of the commander of the 328th Brigade for defence. However, it is entitled "Sabur" because it was made on the basis of the order of the commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what "Sabur" refers to. What is that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It's a code name for this decision of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall, sir, or have any recollection of when Sabur occurred?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date. But if I looked at the different features that we had on the defence lines, I could perhaps set a time on that in terms of several months' span.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could then go to the upper half of the map, and if we could zoom in on the upper half of the map. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we need to zoom in further, sir, we can do that. Can you, based on the lines estimated, give us an approximate time period for this map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It is quite difficult to do that. Let's see feature 702, 705, so that I can -- I can establish whether it was before the 25th of May or after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll over to the right a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The region of Podsjelovo, the area of Podsjelovo is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the Podsjelovo area on this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It's vaguely visible, but I do believe that this reflected the situation before the 25th of May; meaning before the Operation Proljece.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please see the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this map represents.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is the 35th Division's commander's decision for attack and the disposition of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And which operation does this map relate to, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The Farz 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this map represents, sir.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This map reflects one of my decisions for attack operations in the area of Podsjelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could, please, zoom right into the middle of the map where the markings "Odred El Mujahedin" can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, based on the markings on this map, can you give us an approximate date or time period when this map was created.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I cannot. This map is not clear to me, because with parts of my units, I operated in the area of Garici, which is a hamlet of the Imamovici village, where on the 26th or at the end of June and the beginning of July, this major battle took place, the one that I referred to previously. I don't know whether this was a correction of a technical -- tactical position or maybe the objective was something else, so there's very little that I can explain on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, can you tell us, sir, the markings, with respect to the "Odred El Mujahedin," can you explain the three arrows that appear emanating from -- from those words.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: You can see on this map that the objective of the combat activities of the El Mujahedin are the three elevations, 726, 702, and 706.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, earlier this morning, you told us about those three elevation points. Did the El Mujahedin Detachment take those three elevation points?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: On the -- I think it was around the 25th of May - I cannot be specific - 25th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could, please, just zoom out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask you, sir, if you recognise the signature on the bottom right-hand corner of this map.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, based on what you just told us, that you think the El Mujahedin Detachment took the three elevation points, 726, 702, and 706, on -- around 25 May 1995, can you comment on the approximate date of this map, in terms of what's depicted? Would -- would the map have been made before or after the 25th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It was certainly produced before the 25th of May. Had it been produced afterwards, then these three elevation points would have been in my area of responsibility, but I can only speculate as to the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we can finally see the last map in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Wait, hold on. Before we leave this map, I would like to ascertain the implications of this map, because I'm unsure about how the Court should interpret this. Notably, I wish to know whether this map was drawn up as part of an order to the units of the El Mujahid Detachment which were applied in this particular attack and handed down to those units by the witness, or whether the map came about as a result of a message from the El Mujahid Detachment that this is the way they intended to go about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, did you hear the Judge's questions; and if you understood what he's asking you, could you please answer those questions?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I already said, each map accompanied by an order in writing. This map depicts the actions of my units; and, most probably, it was drafted on the basis of the 35th Division commander's order. The El Mujahedin Detachment is my adjacent unit, and this map shows that detachment as an adjacent unit which works in concerted action with my units, but which has nothing to do with me or with my units. Neither do I report to that unit, nor do I send any documents to that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are we to understand, then, that the operation to be carried out by El Mujahid Detachment, which on the map is coloured with a green colour, that this was something that went on completely beyond your control.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While the other action just to the north-west of -- of the El Mujahid action, there are some other actions indicated in the yellow colour. Were, then, these actions under your control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I stated a minute ago, this is the decision of the commander of the 328th Brigade, which was forwarded to the commanders of battalions, and each order is accompanied by a map. You see the area of responsibility of my units; and, primarily, in that operation, I'm interested in my units. Our adjacent unit to the right effected combat operations, but I had no -- apart from being adjacent unit, I had with them no other links.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understood that much. My question is: If the actions coloured in yellow, were actions carried out by soldiers under your command and whether your area of responsibility is indicated as being between the black abrupted lines there -- there's a dot and a line, and a dot and a line marked in black that sort of cuts the front line in two places. My question is whether your area of responsibility was then between these two lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My AOR was between those two lines, but I cannot locate it temporally, this decision. I don't know what it was attached to, whether this was an operation of the 35th Division or whether I wanted by this operation to improve my tactical position, because this concerned the hamlet of the Imamovici village, where we had lost some ground. I don't know which decision this map refers to because there were several decisions, and each decision or order was accompanied by a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, if you also see on this map, to the south-west of the markings "Odred El Mujahedin," we see "4.bb." Do you sigh that, sir? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What do the figures "4.bb" refer to on this map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It refers to the 4th Mountain Battalion of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what that unit was doing in the position south-west of the El Mujahedin Detachment at the time this map was created?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: They were maintaining a decisive defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this map is, sir.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is a map produced by my chief of artillery, Captain Musad Halilovic, whereby he plans activities for offensive actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on the upper right-hand corner, sir, do you recognise the signature on this map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, or can you tell us based upon the markings on the map the approximate time period when this map was created?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Since it's not dated, two versions are possible. One version is 15th of September. I know that this part of the territory had been liberated. But even before that, we had carried out a number of combat activities in this area. We tried to capture the feature Blizna, which we were not successful at. So this could be in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what time period is that when you unsuccessfully tried to capture the feature Blizna?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Throughout the war, on several occasions; maybe seven or eight occasions. But I can tell you that this was before the 15th of September, because the plan concerned division plans for artillery which was sent from chief of artillery of the 35th Division to the chief of artillery of the 328th Brigade to make it an integral part of his plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this collection of six maps into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, this question comes to you. The witness has been telling us that these maps, each one of these maps, goes with an oral order. Can the Court expect that PT2935 -- I beg your pardon, I said "an oral order." A written order. Can the Court expect that PT2935 has written orders that go with each of these maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That -- that is what the witness has told us, Your Honours, but we do not seem to have all of these orders or any of these orders in our possession or on the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is which? Is it all of these orders or any of these orders?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, we have looked for the orders when I was proofing this witness, and we have not been able to -- to locate the orders that go with these -- with these maps. So that leads me to believe either that they are not in our possession; or, if they are in our possession, we have not been able to sufficiently link them with these maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you -- how do you anticipate the Court to comprehend these maps? They are without dates. They are without --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- written orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The witness has given us indications of the approximately dates of the maps. The maps are simply aids to understanding other evidence that has been led or will be led in terms of where units were located, simply to place these various units into locations at approximate time periods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, I have to say that I am increasingly uncomfortable with the way in which evidence is tendered in this trial. This is a general comment that I have not only for the admission of evidence today but also at many previous hearings. Let me take as a example and a starting point your tendering of these six maps into evidence. Apart from the fifth map to which I had some questions to put, I have been unable to understand the meaning of these other remaining five maps, and I am unsure about what evidence the Prosecution expects the Chamber to elicit from these maps combined with the evidence offered -- or the testimony offered by the witness. My suggestion is that if you wish to have these maps tendered, apart from the one that we did look at in detail, you should explain to us what it is you want us to learn from them. The same goes, if I can take some other examples of the documents that you have just previously tendered into evidence, Exhibit 794 and 795, for instance, were the ones that dealt with the EMD units being pulled out of the lines of defence. You can't just leave us there without seeking to -- to clarify just why this is relevant. We have heard earlier in this trial some evidence that point to the consequences of EMD being pulled out of the front lines. My question is now: If these two documents that you have tendered into evidence, and which we have admitted, are relevant to -- to that particular incident or are relevant to something else; and if so, then what? So my general comment is that as much as I understand and appreciate your effort to go quickly and move quickly through this trial, you also have to appreciate the need for the Chamber to be given a better opportunity to understand the meaning and the importance and the significance and the probative -- the probative value of the documents that you put; otherwise, we'll be at a loss. I mean, look at it. We're almost close to 800 exhibits. If we assume that just the average number of pages attached to each of these 800 exhibits amount to five or ten pages, then we are already up looking at a body of evidence halfway through the trial of somewhere between four and eight thousand pages. This is -- this will be extremely difficult for us to grasp in the end when we come to the closure of the trial. So I would therefore urge parties - and it goes for the Defence as well - to be more careful, to make sure that the Chamber has understood what you want to show with all the evidence that you are putting before us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT2935 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll have to dissent from that decision. I will not go along with the admission of these six maps for the reasons that I have just explained. If anything, I will go along with admission of the map number 5 that you exposed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 797.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and I'm going to examine you on behalf of the Defence of General Delic. The nature of cross-examination is such that most of my questions will be answerable by a "yes" or "no." If you, however, do feel the need to provide a broader explanation, please feel free to do so. Since we are speaking the same language and we have this problem with the transcript, please do try and I will try as well to make a break between my question and your answer, so that the transcript can reflect my questions and your answers. Have you understood?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we retrieve the last exhibit that we were shown, and this is -- this will be the departure point for my cross-examination. I believe that this was Exhibit 797.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, asked by the Prosecutor about these maps, you've just provided some explanations. First of all, I would like to ask you as follows: This map represents a schematic of an attack order.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This was for the defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Or defence, as the case may be.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But this is a schematic. Do you agree with me that every map must bear the beginning of combat activities and the end of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this map does not bear any date to end the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please zoom out so that we see the document in its entirety. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain why there are no dates here.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. On the basis of the commander of the 35th Division for defence wherein his order, he determines the areas of responsibility for the defence to our brigades. In my -- in my order, in my decision, I determine which are the areas of responsibility of my battalions with all the elements, such as headquarters, command posts, artillery positions, et cetera. That decision is valid and in effect until the situation out in the field changes. So if we go on attack and we capture new positions, then the decision will be changed, because some unit will have to take the newly reached lines and fortify them, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: So the end, instead of bearing a date, may read: "Until the further commander's decision."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is what is lacking here.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the last map of this -- shown by the Prosecutor, and I believe that this is the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, please, we see map -- ERN number 0466-2140. This is the figure in the top right-hand corner. Do you agree that this map bears no indication of action beginning and action ending?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this should be noted on all maps because all maps reflect a certain combat activity?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would be right in concluding, would I not, that this is a schematic, a map -- a draft of a map which as such was not, in fact, adopted?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We can put this document away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, every time there is a map which does not have the starting date and the closing date of an action, this isn't a map valid for that combat activity because it does not indicate either the date of commencement or the date of ending of a particular combat action. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on to a different topic now. I will go back to the start of your testimony and some questions put to you by the Prosecutor. You gave us some of your professional background information. Am I right in concluding that you did not graduate from the military academy?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The rank of a brigade commander called for an officer, a graduate of a military academy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, in that area, there were no officers of that rank who had been educated or there weren't enough of them.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were very few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. As of March 1993, you were at the head of the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence in Zavidovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained that, for a while, you were a member of the 318th Brigade; and that, upon the establishment of the 328th Brigade, you were appointed its commander. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether in the Zavidovici area there was another commander by the last name of Zilkic, or were you the only one in that area with that family name?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I was the only commander with that family name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Zavidovici area. Very well. The command of your brigade was located in the centre of Zavidovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the 328th Brigade, in the course of 1995, operated within the 35th Division; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Its commander was Mr. Hasanagic, and it also had a command post in Zavidovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to your brigade, part of the 35th Division or subordinated to the 35th Division were also the 327th Maglaj and 329th Kakanj Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there other brigades?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Zavidovici, during the war the civilian authorities were operational, were they not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The public security service was operational, was it not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was at the head of the public security service in 1995 in Zavidovici, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the municipal mayor was in 1995, if you know.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I believe it was Husein Zilkic, but I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Husein Zilkic, is he a relative of yours perhaps?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, extended family.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The municipality had its executive committee, did it not? Do you recall who headed the committee?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nedzad Polic was at the head of the committee, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nedzad Polic. Thank you. I will now be asking you about your today's evidence, above all about the El Mujahedin Detachment. You stated that you met the members of the detachment for the first time in early 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described several encounters and meetings with them, and the Prosecutor showed you documents speaking of joint combat activities carried out by the units in the ground together with the El Mujahedin Detachment, including your unit. Listening to your testimony, I gained the impression that - and I'll please ask you to tell me if I'm right - that the combat activities carried out together with that unit did not present any difficulties. They received your [as interpreted] orders, and they complied with them. Am I right in saying that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you didn't have any problems with them, did you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I had many problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to make a correction of the transcript. At page 69, line 24 I asked the witness: "They received orders, and they complied with them." "Your orders" was entered into the transcript, and I did not say that. So the word "your" should be struck. I didn't put that to the witness, if that can be corrected, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I spoke of other orders, not yours. You understood me correctly, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of them receiving orders from the command of the 35th Division and complying with them, and you replied that, to the best of your understanding, everything worked well. What I want to put to you, however, is this: When it came to other units of the BH army, your adjacent units and brigades, with those units you didn't have any problems; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: With the El Mujahedin Detachment, you did have problems; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These problems were the result of differing outlooks, different views with regard to life and religion when it came to that unit; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your fighters, excluding the fighters of the Camdzic unit which was under you - but I will go back to that unit later on - so excluding that unit, your fighters did have serious problems with that detachment, did they not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you certain documents concerning combat activities and training which was ordered. I will also show you these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can the witness be shown document -- or rather, P2209.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document. This is a document from the security services department of the 3rd Corps sent to the security administration. Please focus on the content. It relates to the training that the El Mujahedin members had with members of your brigade. That's the reason why I'm showing you this document. At some point in your evidence, you stated that the training was carried out according to the plan of the El Mujahedin. Before I invite you to comment upon this document, tell me, sir, did you have an order that the training should be conducted in the way described in this document? Please read the document. I will quote one portion of it which is relevant to us: "Through intelligence work, we have found out that members of the El Mujahedin Unit tried to take advantage of the joint training with members of the 328th Mountain Brigade to win BH army soldiers over." Persons conducting the training are mentioned, and then it says: "The mentioned persons directed all the training towards religion, prayer, and prohibition of alcohol and cigarettes, emphasising that they are on the path of Allah, and at the same time insulting the state leadership and negating our state and the success of the BH army." First, I'll ask you this: Was the order related to such training?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it addressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the order to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Can please the counsel and the witness not overlap. Can the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt here. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry, we were overlapping. I asked you kindly to wait for me to finish my question. I asked you, if you remember, whether the order implied or referred to this part -- this type of training. So please wait for my question before you answer.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The order did not state what sort of training this would be. What I know, based on my knowledge, is that the training was conducted precisely in the manner described in this report. In other words, 95 per cent or 90 per cent of it was religious training, and it was precisely focused on activities such as these. In order to work upon our members, it was to induce them to act as they did, as fighters on the path of Allah. What is not clear from this is that the training was held by the members of the El Mujahid, who were of Bosnian origin from rural areas, who embraced the faith and were very religious but very poorly educated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, you say that they were religious and devout believers, but does this mean that they ought to negate the state leadership and the successes of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No. No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 798.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, I want the witness to be shown document P2144. This document was admitted into evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the exhibit number, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 774.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this document. Will you agree with me that on the 1st of July, 1995, that on that date it was also registered that serious problems were noted during training, where members of your brigade were humiliated, the brigade as such was refuted. There was the -- the flag of the state and the state as such were being offended, and some 25 of your fighters left the training and others announced that they would follow suit?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that such conduct is not something that was typical of the members of the BH army, who normally comply with orders?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were aware of such incidents, were you not, you personally?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: These reports were made on the basis of my reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At this moment, I would like the witness to be shown document D658, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. This is another document of the military security service dated the 21st of March, 1995. It concerns this vandalisation of gravestones on a Serbian cemetery; and in the document, it is said that members of the El Mujahedin Detachment came and destroyed some gravestones. It says, when the soldiers from the 328th Brigade warned them not to do it, the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment removed them under a threat of arms. Does this document describe the event as it happened?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This report was also prepared on the basis of my reports, the reports from my units. My soldiers used to pass this graveyard for more than a year, and it was left intact while they were doing so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I conclude that the detachment members drew weapons and pointed them at your fighters?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this a typical behaviour of a BH army unit to point their weapons at another BH army unit?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: It wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 799.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, may the witness be shown at this moment document D647, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a brief document. Please read it. This is another document of the military security service administration of the army General Staff, dated 20th of July, 1995, describing the conduct of the EMD members. I would like to ask you as follows: In July 1995, the area of Savci and Krivaja --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Salaka [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That area of Salaka-Krivaja was in the AOR of your brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document states that the incident involving the El Mujahedin Detachment members, where they stopped ABiH members, when they were taken towards Paljenik and then released, when they forced their girls to cut each other's hair. You must have heard about this incident.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I did hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document was sent to the State Security Service for investigation most probably, but now I would like to ask you this: Please, sir, in all these documents, we have El Mujahid Detachment members. We don't have none of these perpetrators identified by name.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Out in the field, generally, could you know who those persons were? Could you identify them when such incidents happened?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I must state here that all El Mujahedin Detachment members had arms; whereas, all the weapons of my units was on the line of defence. This is why they could have their way. We could not call anybody, because they were mostly Arabs or they were accompanied by Bosniaks who were part of their detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zilkic, when it comes to those Arabs, as you put it, please, the El Mujahedin Detachment was not the only unit in that area which was peopled by Arabs; in other words, I would like to say this: In the area of Central Bosnia, not only Arabs were part of the El Mujahedin Detachment. There were some other groups. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: There were units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina which had in its composition - and primarily by this I mean the 7th Muslim and 4th Muslim from Konjic, which had such members; there were some other units - but mostly they were in the El Mujahid Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you claim that there were such members in other units, but you were not a member of neither the 7th Muslim, neither the -- nor the 4th Brigade from Konjica. So you don't know what was the relationship between the Arabs in those units.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Correct, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But my question is: You personally did not hear of other Arab groups, apart from the El Mujahedin Detachment in this area.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I did not hear of any establishment of any group that would be organised. A unit, should I put it this way? I did not hear that there was any other unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the 5th Battalion -- or your 5th Battalion was headquartered at Imamovici; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was it headquartered?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: The 5th Battalion was -- had its main command post at Borovnice and forward command post at Mramorje when it was working in that direction. But when it was complete, battalion at its forward command post at Curici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. But you mentioned that you had your communications centre in Imamovici?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you visit that CC ever?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That communications centre was established only for that operation; and after that, it was moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the area of Imamovici?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did go to Imamovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any Arab unit that you would know of?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we put this -- can we tender this document into evidence. May it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 800.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And at this point, may we show the witness the document P2238.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look. This is another military service -- military security service administration document, dated 29th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is not that document, Your Honours, at all. It's 2238.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P2238. This one is okay. Thank you. I will correct myself. This is the right document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is another document by the security service department, dated the 15th of July, 1995, describing the conduct of the El Mujahedin Detachment members in the zone of responsibility of the 328th Brigade, and it describes an event. This is a brief document, sir. Could you please take a look at it. It describes an encounter of your fighters with the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment on the line of defence. I'm going to quote the relevant portion, the last sentence of the third paragraph, and say: "They killed -- they entered the trench and started shouting that this was not the way to guard the line, that they were worse than the Chetniks, as they do not bow, and they just like -- they shave just like the Chetniks; and, moreover, they said that the next time that they will kill them, the soldiers, if they find them not doing the prayers." The "namas" or the prayers is a prayer.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document shows that your soldiers were threatened by them, that they would be killed if they did not engage in prayer.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document depicts a real-life event that you know of.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I heard of this event.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 801.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, now, Witness, I would like to ask you this: The Prosecutor showed you a number of documents which concern joint combat activities, and you said that the 35th Division issued orders. However, regardless of orders on joint combat activities that you saw, it would be fair to say that those documents do not reflect the real state of affairs in the relationship between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the superior commands of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That would be a fair assumption or conclusion.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Such a conclusion can be drawn.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that you testified - and I will be showing you this later in my cross-examination - the 35th Division planned combat activities in July and September. Did I understood you -- did I understand you correctly that you received orders from them?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received all my orders from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, those orders encompassed also the El Mujahedin Detachment, as you said. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that the El Mujahedin Detachment planned their combat activities on their own?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: In reality, out on the ground, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because your reports show - and I'm going to revisit them at a later point - when it says "we proceeded as per El Mujahedin's plans"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is because they did not trust the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they reconnoitered the ground themselves. They did not trust the preparations on the part of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina when it came to combat operations. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So they did their own reconnaissance, did they not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: They did, but they always requested my engineers, "sapas," to remove the land-mines if they were in front of our lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. But they did not accept your suggestions or your intelligence drawn from reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From their participation in combat activities, they made conditional on many requests, and you were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, one of such conditions was that they themselves should determine when an action should start.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes. When they were ready, then we would launch our attacks or actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were brigade commander. Could you make such conditions, impose such conditions? Did other units impose such conditions?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No. What we could do was to report whether we are ready or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: We received orders from our superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you carried out orders, did you not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not impose any conditions on the start of an action or such-like.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actions that had already been planned were pushed back because they would not take part in -- in such an action at a designated time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you document PT2450.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we bring it onto the screen, please, far moment, and that would be Exhibit 793, Your Honours. Exhibit 793.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to take a look at it. This is a document dated the 25th of August, 1995. Do you remember this document had to do with re-subordination? I want to ask you the following: You were ordered in this particular situation; and in several other occasions that you testified to the date, you were ordered to second a number of soldiers belonging to your units. Now, which soldiers you would re-subordinate to them was not a decision that lay entirely in your hands. They also placed certain conditions in that regard. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Specifically speaking of my brigade, yes, as far as offensive activities were concerned. Now, when it came to seconding men to evacuate the wounded, this is something that my battalion commanders would decide upon, because they selected men who were less fit for fighting but could be used to do that part of the job.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mention "offensive activities," and you say that was the case when it comes to offensive activities. I want the Trial Chamber to understand what you're saying. It is true, is it not, that they were prepared to receive as reinforcement in combat activities only the members of your Asim Camdzic unit.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Not only them; sometimes I received an order to second a larger number of men for offensive activities, in addition to Asim Camdzic. Again, it was down to battalion commanders to choose the men who were the fittest for combat, and not those who were -- who had high religious fervor.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you're saying is they accepted those fighters, too.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was based on your statement, Mr. Zilkic, that you gave to the OTP investigators, where you said that they only accepted the fighters from the Asim Camdzic unit. That was the reason why I put this question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will find what the reference is, Your Honours, and we'll revisit the issue some other day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to something else now. Let us clarify the issue of the Asim Camdzic unit. You will agree with me that they -- that, actually, the El Mujahedin Unit placed more trust in the Asim Camdzic unit than in others.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what this means, "they placed more trust in them." They always sought for them to come as reinforcement in activities, and they knew that they -- the unit was composed of religious men. They did not put any additional questions about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These were the men who wore beards, they prayed, they had insignia.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: But -- they did have beards, but they did not have any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not even the religious ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're overlapping please. Both of you don't wait for the other. Madam Vidovic, I would expect at least you to remember this better than the witness, because you are in this every day. The witness is here only today, and he may forget to pause. Please do pause yourself, and could you pause two seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I will be finishing soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we spoke of the Asim Camdzic Unit. You have agreed with me that the unit was composed of men who had beards, who imitated Arabs in their outward appearance and behaviour. Please wait for my question to be finished.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC
utterances.text: I can say that they were all bearded, they engaged in daily prayers, and they resembled Arabs, although they were our members.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suggest that I interrupt my cross-examination at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Sir, unfortunately, we have come to the end of the day for purposes of our case today. We are not done with you. You will have to come back on Tuesday, the 13th of November at quarter past 2.00. We are not going to be sitting on Monday, unfortunately. I'm sorry about this. We had hoped that we could finish with you, and you could get home -- go home before the weekend, but we've got to make space for another case. Okay? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Court will adjourn to Tuesday, the 13th of November at quarter past 2.00, in the same courtroom, II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
